paper_sections.title: Neural representations of relevant and irrelevant features in perceptual decision making
Main effects of task and stimulus type
Attention and accumulation in the frontal and parietal lobes

description.value: The study examined how selective attention to motion versus color changes neural representations of attended and ignored stimulus features during perceptual decision making, using fMRI, modeling, and connectivity analyses.

design.value: Five highly trained human subjects performed a fully crossed motion/color coherence discrimination task during six functional MRI task sessions. Across runs, subjects attended either motion direction or predominant color while ignoring the other feature; separate motion and color localizer tasks and independent training-session data were used for ROI definition.

description.value: Subjects' proportion of correct motion-direction or predominant-color decisions.
Time from stimulus onset to the subject's button-press response.
The coherence level at 75% accuracy as defined by the fitted diffusion model parameters.

source_definition.value: The proportion of dots assigned coherent motion; six levels were used in the fMRI experiment, including a 0% coherence control and individually calibrated levels.

levels.value: 0%, and subject-specific coherence values predicted to produce 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100% accuracy

source_definition.value: The proportion of dots assigned the selected color; six levels were used in the fMRI experiment, including a 0% coherence control and individually calibrated levels.

levels.value: 0%, and subject-specific coherence values predicted to produce 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100% accuracy

source_definition.value: The feature cued for the subject to attend during a run: motion or color.
The stimulus feature that was present but irrelevant to the current task: motion during the color task or color during the motion task.
Mean reaction times for the attend-motion and ignore-motion conditions were inputs to the MT+ attention model.
A′, bearing on the decision threshold.
k, a constant describing the relationship between the motion coherence in the stimulus and the mean drift rate in the model.
TR, the mean residual time in seconds, representing a fixed processing duration independent of evidence accumulation.

description.value: Five subjects, ages 26–38; two males. All subjects had normal neuroanatomy, were right-handed, and had normal or corrected-to-normal vision.

consented_count.value: five subjects gave written informed consent

enrolled_count.value: Five subjects participated in the study

inclusion_criteria.value: normal neuroanatomy as reviewed by a neurologist

task_description.value: Subjects viewed multiple colored moving dots containing independently varying motion coherence and color proportion. At the beginning of each run they were cued to attend either the overall direction of motion or the predominant color while ignoring the other feature, and made a two-alternative forced-choice response.

design_type.value: fully crossed factorial design with independent parametric variation of attended and ignored features

instructions.value: For attend-motion trials, identify the direction of motion as quickly and accurately as possible. For attend-color trials, identify the predominant color as quickly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: Multiple colored moving dots within a central circular aperture of 7.5° diameter; a subset of dots moved coherently leftward or rightward on a background of randomly moving dots, and an uncorrelated subset of dots of one color, blue or red, was present on a background of evenly apportioned blue and red dots.

task_description.value: Subjects viewed 10 repetitions of a 40 s trial in which a motion stimulus was present for 10 s, followed by 30 s of a static dot display.

stimuli.value: Ten consecutive 1 s presentations of 100% dot motion coherence with directions chosen randomly without replacement from [0, 36, 72, … 324°], followed by a static dot display.

task_description.value: Subjects viewed 10 repetitions of a 40 s trial consisting of a 10 s color stimulus followed by a 30 s grayscale stimulus.

stimuli.value: Ten consecutive 1 s stationary displays of colored squares subtending 0.57° at a density of 16.7 squares/deg2, followed by the same type of stimulus shown in grayscale.

task_name.value: subject training and eye movement training

task_description.value: Subjects completed a minimum of nine 1.5 h training sessions before scanning, including separate motion and color training and training with both features present. Eye movement training instructed subjects to maintain fixation and refrain from blinking.

instructions.value: Maintain an eye position within 3° of the fixation cross and refrain from blinking throughout the duration of the stimulus regardless of the response time.

stimuli.value: Motion and color coherence stimuli containing separate or combined features.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3T MR Scanner at the Henry H. Wheeler, Jr., Brain Imaging Center at the University of California, Berkeley

description.value: Functional images consisted of 24 slices acquired with a gradient echoplanar imaging protocol. Six functional MRI task sessions were conducted, each consisting of eight runs of 48 trials.
Anatomical images consisted of 160 slices acquired using a T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid-acquisition gradient echo protocol.

instrument.value: ASL Eye-Trac 6 LRO; ViewPoint Eye Tracker (Close-Focus Camera and Illuminator)

description.value: Eye movement data were acquired for three subjects at the Neuroimaging Center at the University of California, San Francisco Medical Center and for two subjects during training sessions at the University of California, Berkeley.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: Eye tracking is not MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET.

description.value: Functional images were converted to 4D NIfTI format, slice-time corrected, motion corrected, spatially smoothed, coregistered to the structural image, and normalized to MNI_N27 space.

steps.value: Functional images were converted to 4D NIfTI format.
Images were corrected for slice-timing offsets.
Motion correction was performed using AFNI 3dvolreg, with the reference volume set to the mean image of the first run in the series.
Images were smoothed with a 5 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.
Coregistration was performed with AFNI 3dAllineate using the local Pearson correlation cost function optimized for fMRI-to-MRI structural alignment.
The inverse transformation was used to warp the anatomical image to functional image space.
Anatomical images were normalized using FSL fnirt to the standard MNI_N27 volume.
The same normalization parameters were applied to native-space statistical maps as necessary for group statistical maps.

model_settings.value: The model fit reaction time and accuracy data with three variables: A′, k, and TR. Fits were determined separately for attend-motion and attend-color conditions.

estimator.value: Iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood (Lp) of the diffusion model fit.

hrf_model.value: γ probability density function peaking at 6 s

model_settings.value: Separate regressors modeled six levels of motion coherence, six levels of color coherence, and the attended/ignored feature. Each regressor was convolved with the γ probability density function and stimulus onsets. Linear trends were tested using coherence contrast vectors transformed to zero mean and a sum of squares equal to 1.

The voxelwise t statistic was divided by the square root of the number of subjects (n = 5) and compared against a standard normal null distribution. Significance required p = 0.001 for the full group and a significant effect at p < 0.05 in at least three of five subjects.

estimator.value: fixed-effects analysis with an overlap requirement

model_type.value: random-effects t test and repeated-measures ANOVA

model_settings.value: ROI-extracted peak amplitudes and time-to-peak values were evaluated using random-effects t tests or repeated-measures ANOVA.
Piecewise b-spline basis functions were separated by 2 s intervals for 20 s after stimulus onset.

The MT+ BOLD response was modeled as bottom-up input multiplied by an attentional factor. The attentional factor differed from baseline for the duration of the reaction time and returned to baseline thereafter; bottom-up input persisted for the 2500 ms stimulus duration and was assumed to be the same for a given motion coherence regardless of attention.

model_type.value: Granger causality using multivariate autoregressive models

model_settings.value: Detrended fMRI time courses were averaged across voxels in each ROI. Granger causality values were computed between V4, MT+, mIPS, and IFS for each run, divided into smaller sets of 35 TRs. Conditional Granger causality was also computed by conditioning on IFS or mIPS activity.

estimator.value: multivariate autoregressive prediction; Wilcoxon's two-sided signed rank test

description.value: Subjects identified leftward or rightward motion while ignoring the color feature.
Subjects identified the predominant red or blue color while ignoring the motion feature.
A 100% coherent dot-motion stimulus was presented for 10 s.
A static dot display was presented for 30 s between motion stimuli.
Stationary displays of fully saturated colored squares were presented for 10 s.
The same type of color-localizer stimulus was shown in grayscale for 30 s between color displays.

definition.value: Hard > easy, corresponding to a negative parametric variation with attended motion coherence; the relevant coherence vector was transformed to zero mean and a sum of squares equal to 1.

interpretations.value: BOLD activity varied negatively with attended motion coherence in the mIPS, IFS, anterior insula, and other regions.

definition.value: Hard > easy, corresponding to a negative parametric variation with attended color coherence; the relevant coherence vector was transformed to zero mean and a sum of squares equal to 1.

interpretations.value: BOLD activity varied negatively with attended color coherence in the mIPS, IFS, anterior insula, and other regions.

title.value: Areas showing significant univariate activity during performance of the task, in MNI coordinates

footer.value: The top section lists those regions that demonstrated a significant parametric effect with respect to attended motion coherence; note that the direction of the parametric effect (positive or negative) is indicated by the sign of the associated T value. In the middle section are listed those areas showing a significant parametric effect for ignored motion coherence, and in the bottom section can be seen those regions demonstrating a significant parametric effect of attended color coherence. Each of the three sections (top, middle, bottom) only includes areas whose main effect of task was positive (i.e., that activated during stimulus presentation). “Overlap” indicates the number of individual subjects who showed significant univariate effects within each region. No regions demonstrated a significant parametric effect of ignored color coherence. SFG, Superior frontal gyrus; aIPS, anterior intraparietal sulcus; SMA, supplementary motor area; PMC, premotor cortex; pIPS, posterior intraparietal sulcus; MFG, middle frontal gyrus; pOCC, posterior occipital cortex; ACC, anterior cingulate cortex; pMTG, posterior middle temporal gyrus; STG, superior temporal gyrus; dOCC, dorsal occipital cortex; pMFG, posterior middle frontal gyrus; vOCC, ventral occipital cortex.
